admissions.why: Year-end archive clears the active class only after successful creation/upload/download. A Drive folder-create response without an ID, a tiny resolved ZIP, or an initially signed-out call must not cross that boundary. Existing archive-failures tests distinguish failed compression/download and missing FILE upload IDs, but their folder mocks always return IDs; archive-connection tests switch an existing connection, not initial sign-out. Missing-folder and invalid-size success results are different failure shapes from a rejected compression promise. These checks protect writing/class state even though the current source already contains the right guards.

admissions.why: Ordinary users choose the OCR region by dragging. Current strong ownership/pixel tests assign _cropRect directly, and script-loading only opens the modal then presses Escape. Neither proves mouse/touch coordinate conversion, reverse drag or drag termination. A wrong region can produce the wrong writing/OCR image while all current pixel/ownership cases pass; original preservation makes this recoverable, but the missing native event-to-pixel contract has real correctness value.

admissions.smallest_existing_suite_change: Add two adjacent native event cases to tests/crop-transparency.browser.cjs, reusing its real PNG acquisition, native Image decode, pixel sampling and reset helpers. Keep its existing4 opaque/transparent/reset cases and the entire crop-ownership suite. Open through the visible Crop button; do not assign _cropRect. Use one mouse drag and one browser touch sequence/reverse drag at a scaled rendered size, with document release and a later move that must not alter the final region.
admissions.substantive_oracle: Use the existing asymmetric ink/background fixture or a tiny asymmetric raster. Assert independent literal output dimensions AND ink/background pixels at known source-relative points with the existing JPEG tolerance. Dimensions alone cannot detect a shifted rectangle. Also require the exact original bytes retained, only the intended image changed, stale Drive reference cleared/revision advanced and OCR cache invalidated; preserve owner/writing/pending/source state. Inspect actual getBoundingClientRect for input placement, but do not compute expected output by calling getCropPos or duplicating its implementation.

retained_or_deferred.scope: empty/stale selection, empty portfolio, whitespace year and school-year month boundary
retained_or_deferred.reason: These are explicit no-op/error/compatibility boundaries, not evidence of lost data. The current portfolio navigation tests assert valid populated selection and export enabled; empty selection is ordinarily gated by the disabled UI. Keep helper rejection for stale data without manufacturing a user bug. Empty student HTML is an explanatory document; January/July labels affect naming rather than ownership or clearing. Blank-year/cancel returns precede archive work. They can gain cheap tests later, but are below the admitted IO and native-crop gaps.

retained_or_deferred.scope: post-clipping minimum-size guard and optional DOM/backdrop branches
retained_or_deferred.reason: With stable loaded canvas dimensions, both drag endpoints are clamped, so a nominal >=5px region cannot become smaller merely through the later clipping calculation. Keep the second guard for changed-canvas/preload or nonstandard caller state; do not inject an impossible normal drag just to hit144-145. Existing initial3px/preload cases cover distinct contracts. Backdrop/optional missing-DOM behavior is lower risk; keep it without a new generic harness.

Do not add another generic upload-failure/connection race matrix: real photo/ZIP bytes, all-or-nothing requested-photo failures, current-work snapshot retention, connection changes at async stages, missing FILE acknowledgement, required storage failure/retry and postcommit UI failures already have substantive assertions in archive-integrity, archive-failures and archive-connection. Missing FOLDER acknowledgement is the distinct admitted gap.
